Diagnosis and fix are complete and verified. The full markdown solution is at **`/workspace/solution.md`**; the referenced library is also at `/tmp/qa-fix/qa-repo-sanity.sh` and the suite at `/tmp/qa-fix/tests/run.sh`.

## Summary

**Root cause:** The QA launcher only classified a launch dir as "git toplevel" (grade it) or "subdirectory of a repo" (refuse). A stand-in lane is a git subdirectory of a foreign parent meta-repo, so the launcher either synced/graded the parent (wrong product) or died on `is a SUBDIRECTORY of git repo <parent>`. It never consulted the stand-in's `<dir>/.coding-hermes/board` symlink, which points into the real product repo.

**Fix:** A shared `bunker_qa_resolve_repo_root()` with strict precedence:
1. `BUNKER_QA_SUBDIR` explicit override (absolute or relative) — always wins.
2. Stand-in board-symlink resolution: `readlink -f <dir>/.coding-hermes/board` → target dir's `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` → require `product_top != parent_top`, `product_top != launch_dir`, and exact round-trip; emit a loud `NOTE` naming launch dir, product root and symlink target.
3. Named refusal — unchanged original guard, reached only when neither applies (same-parent, non-repo, broken/self symlinks, plain subdirs).

Plus a read-only `bunker-qa resolve <repo-dir>` subcommand that prints only the decision, no agent spawn.

**Verification (actually run):**

```
TOTAL: 36  PASS: 36  FAIL: 0
```

Covers positive resolution, override precedence/normalization/validation, and all negatives: same-parent symlink, non-repo target, broken symlink, self-target, plain-subdir refusal with the single FAIL evidence row, and a `$PATH` `bunker` stub proving `resolve` spawns no agent. The solution doc includes the full drop-in library, integration patch points, the complete test runner, and live read-only probe usage.

The durable fix (bunker commit ab23c36b, QA-BUNKER-REVIEW-3): a shared repo-sanity function with precedence explicit BUNKER_QA_SUBDIR override > stand-in board-symlink product-root resolution > named refusal. The resolution reads <dir>/.coding-hermes/board (stand-in lanes symlink their board into the real product repo), readlink -f's it, takes the target directory's git rev-parse --show-toplevel, verifies product_top != parent git_top and that it round-trips as a toplevel, then syncs/grades that root with a loud NOTE naming launch dir, resolved root and symlink target; same-parent or non-repo targets fall through to the original refusal (no bogus resolution). A safe 'resolve <repo-dir>' subcommand prints the decision with no agent spawn, which makes the fix testable offline (fixture repos) and live-provable read-only. Tests: 36 offline git-fixture checks incl. negative cases (same-parent symlink, non-repo symlink target, plain subdir refusal with one FAIL evidence row).
